process_observations.observation: Both directions of the manifest/file consistency check still pass over the whole build tree after the rebuild: 57 members all resolve to files and all 64 deployable files under artefacts/ are covered by a member, counting the seven -meta.xml siblings that travel with their bodies.

The evidence behind this manifest's Apex members moved from compile-only to actually executing and passing between the prior build of this file and this rebuild: reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md run 8 shows 4/4 CaseMilestoneServiceTest methods passing at 84.4% coverage, with F-59, F-60, F-61 and F-62 all closed by the org.

reports/MILESTONE-M5-package.xml is a snapshot written by agents/milestone-verifier before this rebuild and states in its own header that it is 'identical to artefacts/M5-S05/package.xml - 29 types, 56 members'. That claim is now false: this file carries 57 members. The snapshot is stale, not this agent's to edit (milestone-verifier owns it), and the drift is a milestone-level re-verification trigger.

F-60's fix (fieldPermissions added to Case_Agent_Core) is a content-only change to a file this manifest already names as a member. A manifest diff alone would never have surfaced F-60 or F-61 or F-62 -- all three were found by the org actually running the test, not by any checker or manifest check in this build. The manifest/file consistency check this agent runs is necessary but was never going to be sufficient for this class of defect.

M4-S05's own outputs[] in plan.json still lists 8 paths (through TestDataFactory) and has not been amended to add TestUserFactory.cls / .cls-meta.xml, even though both files exist on disk and this manifest now cites TestUserFactory as a member. This agent reads M4-S05's artefacts directory directly (per its own Mandatory Reads and Step 4's upstream-artefacts source), not its outputs[] declaration, so the member is grounded either way -- but a human reading plan.json alone would not see the file listed as a declared output of the step that produced it.
